html:
What this means for your business

The goal is not a magic policy. It is a small rule everyone can follow when they are busy: protect private information, check the result, and ask before sending something important.

What to watch

  • Customer, employee, payment, password, health, legal, or tax details pasted into a public AI tool.
  • An AI answer copied into a customer message without a person checking it.
  • A new paid tool bought before the business names the job it should help with.
  • Nobody able to explain what information enters the tool or who approves the result.

Do this next

  1. Pick one low-risk task, such as a first draft or a list of public questions.
  2. Write down what information must stay out of the tool.
  3. Name the person who checks the result before it reaches a customer.
  4. Keep, change, or stop after a small trial based on time saved and mistakes found.

When Little Fight fits

We can map a safe, useful use for AI around the tools you already have. We do not hand customer promises or important business decisions to a machine.

insight.answer: Use AI for low-risk drafts and sorting. Keep private business information out. A person still checks important facts and every customer promise.
